description: Team TERRA LUNA - Finding the Moon and Mars on Earth. We use open NASA, ISRO, and ESA Earth, Moon, and Mars data to identify and characterize new terrestrial analog sites like deserts, volcanic terrains, polar regions, and caves to test and validate future lunar base and landing site technologies.
summary:
The platform brings together Earth terrain information and geographic visualization to examine environments such as high-altitude mountains, arid deserts, and volcanic landscapes. Users can explore candidate locations through an interactive map and view terrain information, including elevation, slope, and local relief.

The current prototype focuses on processing NASADEM elevation data for the Ladakh region and presenting the resulting terrain analysis through an interactive web interface. It also identifies other candidate environments, including the Atacama Desert and Hawaiian volcanic terrain, for further investigation.

TERRATWIN aims to provide a foundation for comparing terrestrial environments with lunar and Martian terrain datasets in future development. Its long-term goal is to make planetary analogue research more accessible through interactive maps, terrain analysis, and clear scientific data visualization.
details: TERRATWIN, developed by Project Terra Luna 2K26, is an AI-inspired planetary analogue discovery system created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project aims to identify and explore locations on Earth that share environmental and terrain characteristics with the Moon and Mars, helping researchers understand where future space-exploration technologies could be tested before being deployed on other worlds. Through an interactive web-based map and terrain visualizations, TERRATWIN presents candidate locations such as Ladakh in India, the Atacama Desert in Chile, and volcanic basalt landscapes in Hawaii. It uses NASA Earth elevation data, including NASADEM, to examine terrain features such as elevation, slope, and surface relief, while providing information about relevant planetary data sources such as the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) and Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) for future integration. By combining Earth observation, geospatial analysis, and interactive visualization, TERRATWIN aims to make the search for Earth-based testing environments more accessible and support the preparation of future lunar and Martian missions.
